requirements.requirement: /tmp mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev all enforced
requirements.summary: fstab entry added for /tmp with defaults,noexec,nosuid,nodev; mounted live (cmd-8614c89e44b84a61) showing rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec; functionally verified exec blocked (Permission denied, rc=126) and nodev blocked (mknod succeeded but open denied) on /tmp (cmd-537252197f3340e1, cmd-171855d7b3c24992). Setuid bit was set but not independently isolated from noexec, though the nosuid mount option itself is directly confirmed present via findmnt.

requirements.requirement: /dev/shm mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev all enforced
requirements.summary: fstab entry added for /dev/shm; remounted live (cmd-8614c89e44b84a61) showing rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec; exec denied and device-node open denied on /dev/shm (cmd-537252197f3340e1, cmd-171855d7b3c24992).

Pre-restart boot_id and mount state captured (cmd-70e22b898e184885, boot_id 636556ce...), reboot triggered and acknowledged (cmd-f6de0fc62b8749e5), connectivity loss observed during the transition (cmd-41624617417f4f72, cmd-deaeaaca24fd4963, cmd-95741bd434ba40ee), new boot_id confirmed post-reboot (cmd-83bbdaeb99ce4c63, 0e7ec19c...), and post-reboot findmnt plus functional exec/device-node tests confirm the options and enforcement persisted (cmd-894c09923da1422f). This satisfies the required pre-baseline/disruption/restoration/recovered-state transition for a persistence claim.

overall_summary: The executor correctly added persistent fstab entries giving /tmp and /dev/shm the noexec,nosuid,nodev options, applied them live, and directly demonstrated enforcement (blocked script execution, blocked device-node reads) on both mounts before and after a full reboot with a verified boot-identity change, satisfying all three material outcomes of the task with a complete baseline→disruption→recovery evidence chain.
limitations: Setuid (nosuid) enforcement was not isolated from noexec in the functional tests — a setuid binary was created but not actually re-executed to trigger suid-drop behavior specifically, since exec was already blocked; the nosuid mount option's presence in findmnt output is used as the primary evidence for that sub-requirement.
A backup file /etc/fstab.bak.<timestamp> was left on the node; this is low-risk residue not explicitly cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: All mutating commands map clearly to the task: fstab backup+append (cmd-6534a047292b4059), live mount/remount (cmd-8614c89e44b84a61), functional test artifacts on /tmp and /dev/shm (scripts, setuid copy, mknod device nodes) created in cmd-537252197f3340e1 and cmd-894c09923da1422f were fully removed by matching cleanup commands (cmd-171855d7b3c24992, cmd-894c09923da1422f), and the reboot (cmd-f6de0fc62b8749e5) was a necessary, bounded, single-node action directly required to prove persistence per the task contract. One minor residue: a timestamped /etc/fstab.bak.<timestamp> backup file was left on node1 (created within cmd-6534a047292b4059) — a reasonable safety precaution before editing fstab, not a harmful mutation, but not cleaned up. No failed services, no unnecessary network exposure, no damaged package state; global lifecycle comparison shows no unexpected changes beyond the reboot-driven boot id, ephemeral systemd-private tmp dirs, and sshd/chronyd PID changes.
